metadata.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Unsupervised Token Corpus
nodes.statement: An unsupervised corpus of tokens $\mathcal{U} = \{u_1, \dots, u_n\}$ used to train the language model.
nodes.statement_clean: Unlabeled token sequence used as the pre-training corpus.

nodes.name: Labeled Target Dataset
nodes.statement: A labeled dataset $\mathcal{C}$ where each instance is a sequence of input tokens $x^1, \dots, x^m$ together with a label $y$.
nodes.statement_clean: Supervised target dataset of token sequences with labels.

nodes.name: Transformer Decoder Block
nodes.statement: A multi-layer Transformer decoder applying multi-headed self-attention over input context tokens followed by position-wise feedforward layers; defined recursively by $h_0 = U W_e + W_p$, $h_l = \mathrm{transformer\_block}(h_{l-1})$ for $l \in [1,n]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stacked self-attention plus feedforward blocks producing layer-wise hidden states.
nodes.origin_citation: Vaswani et al., Attention is all you need, 2017; Liu et al. 2018

nodes.name: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) Vocabulary
nodes.statement: A subword vocabulary built via byte-pair encoding with $40{,}000$ merges, used to tokenize the input text.
nodes.statement_clean: Subword tokenization using BPE with 40K merges.

nodes.name: Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU)
nodes.statement: Activation function used throughout the model, bridging nonlinearities and stochastic regularizers.
nodes.statement_clean: GELU activation used in the Transformer.

nodes.name: Language Modeling Objective $L_1$
nodes.statement: $L_1(\mathcal{U}) = \sum_i \log P(u_i \mid u_{i-k}, \dots, u_{i-1}; \Theta)$, where $k$ is the context window size and $P$ is parameterized by a neural network with parameters $\Theta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximize the log-likelihood of each token given the previous k tokens.

nodes.name: Transformer Forward Pass
nodes.statement: $h_0 = U W_e + W_p$; $h_l = \mathrm{transformer\_block}(h_{l-1})\ \forall l \in [1,n]$; $P(u) = \mathrm{softmax}(h_n W_e^T)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recursive Transformer hidden states with tied embedding output projection.

nodes.name: Supervised Prediction Distribution
nodes.statement: $P(y \mid x^1, \dots, x^m) = \mathrm{softmax}(h_l^m W_y)$, where $h_l^m$ is the final transformer block's activation on the last token and $W_y$ is the added linear output layer.
nodes.statement_clean: Class probability obtained by softmax over the final hidden state times added output weights.

nodes.name: Supervised Objective $L_2$
nodes.statement: $L_2(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{(x,y)} \log P(y \mid x^1, \dots, x^m)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sum of log-likelihoods of labels over the supervised dataset.

nodes.name: Combined Fine-tuning Objective $L_3$
nodes.statement: $L_3(\mathcal{C}) = L_2(\mathcal{C}) + \lambda \cdot L_1(\mathcal{C})$, where $\lambda$ weights the auxiliary language modeling loss during fine-tuning.
nodes.statement_clean: Fine-tuning loss combining the supervised loss with a weighted language modeling auxiliary loss.

nodes.name: Semi-supervised Language Understanding
nodes.statement: Learn a universal text representation from a large unlabeled corpus and adapt it with little task-specific change to a wide range of supervised target tasks (NLI, QA, similarity, classification).
nodes.statement_clean: Build one model that pre-trains on raw text and transfers to many supervised NLP tasks.

nodes.name: Generative Pre-Training + Discriminative Fine-Tuning
nodes.statement: Two-stage training: first maximize the language modeling objective $L_1$ on unlabeled tokens, then maximize the combined objective $L_3 = L_2 + \lambda L_1$ on each labeled target task using task-specific input transformations.
nodes.statement_clean: Pre-train Transformer LM, then fine-tune with auxiliary LM loss on each task.
input: Transformer architecture (12 layers, 768 dim, 12 heads, 3072 inner)
output: Fine-tuned classifier weights $W_y$ for each task

nodes.name: Unsupervised Pre-training
nodes.statement: Train the multi-layer Transformer decoder on $\mathcal{U}$ by maximizing $L_1(\mathcal{U}) = \sum_i \log P(u_i \mid u_{i-k}, \dots, u_{i-1}; \Theta)$ via stochastic gradient descent.

nodes.name: Apply Task-Specific Input Transformation
nodes.statement: Convert each structured task input (entailment pair, similarity pair, QA tuple) into a single contiguous token sequence with delimiter token \$ and randomly initialized $\langle s \rangle, \langle e \rangle$ start/end tokens.

nodes.name: Add Linear Output Head and Fine-tune
nodes.statement: Pass inputs through the pre-trained model to obtain $h_l^m$, add a linear output layer $W_y$ giving $P(y \mid x^1,\dots,x^m) = \mathrm{softmax}(h_l^m W_y)$, and maximize the combined objective $L_3 = L_2 + \lambda L_1$ on the labeled task data.

nodes.name: Return Fine-tuned Model
nodes.statement: Return the fine-tuned parameters $(\Theta, W_y)$ together with the embeddings of any added delimiter tokens.

nodes.name: Task-Specific Input Transformations
nodes.statement: Traversal-style scheme that converts structured task inputs into a single token sequence using delimiter token \$ and start/end tokens $\langle s \rangle, \langle e \rangle$, so the pre-trained Transformer needs minimal architectural changes per task.
input: Structured task input (premise/hypothesis pair, sentence pair, or document/question/answers)
Start token $\langle s \rangle$ and end token $\langle e \rangle$
output: A single contiguous token sequence consumable by the pre-trained Transformer

nodes.name: Textual Entailment Encoding
nodes.statement: For an entailment task, concatenate premise $p$ and hypothesis $h$ token sequences with a delimiter token \$ in between: $[\langle s \rangle; p; \$; h; \langle e \rangle]$.

nodes.name: Similarity Encoding
nodes.statement: For similarity, encode both possible orderings of the two sentences with a delimiter, run each through the model independently, and add their final representations $h_l^m$ element-wise before the linear output layer.

nodes.name: QA / Commonsense Encoding
nodes.statement: Given context document $z$, question $q$, and answer set $\{a_k\}$, form sequences $[z; q; \$; a_k]$ for each $k$, run each independently through the model, and normalize via softmax to produce a distribution over answers.

nodes.name: Adam Optimizer
nodes.statement: Adaptive moment-estimation optimizer used to train the model with max learning rate $2.5 \times 10^{-4}$, linear warmup over the first 2000 updates, and cosine annealing to zero.

nodes.name: BooksCorpus Pre-training
nodes.statement: Pre-train the 12-layer Transformer LM on BooksCorpus (over 7{,}000 unpublished books with long stretches of contiguous text), achieving a token-level perplexity of $18.4$.

nodes.name: NLI Benchmarks (MNLI, SNLI, SciTail, QNLI, RTE)
nodes.statement: Apply the fine-tuned Transformer LM to five NLI datasets; achieves absolute gains up to $1.5\%$ on MNLI, $5\%$ on SciTail, $5.8\%$ on QNLI, and $0.6\%$ on SNLI over previous best, while underperforming on the smallest set RTE ($56\%$ vs $61.7\%$).

nodes.name: Question Answering (RACE, Story Cloze)
nodes.statement: Fine-tuned Transformer LM achieves $86.5\%$ on Story Cloze and $59.0\%$ on RACE, outperforming previous best by $8.9\%$ on Story Cloze and $5.7\%$ on RACE.

nodes.name: Semantic Similarity (MRPC, QQP, STS-B)
nodes.statement: Achieves SOTA on two of three semantic similarity datasets with $1$-point absolute gain on STS-B and $4.2\%$ absolute improvement on QQP F1 over Single-task BiLSTM + ELMo + Attn.

nodes.name: Classification (CoLA, SST-2) and GLUE
nodes.statement: Achieves Matthews correlation $45.4$ on CoLA (vs previous best $35.0$), accuracy $91.3\%$ on SST-2, and an overall GLUE score of $72.8$ (vs previous best $68.9$).

nodes.name: Layer Transfer Analysis
nodes.statement: Transferring an increasing number of pre-trained Transformer layers to MultiNLI/RACE yields monotone gains, with up to $9\%$ improvement on MultiNLI for full transfer.

nodes.name: Zero-shot Heuristic Tasks
nodes.statement: Heuristic zero-shot evaluations using only the generative model (CoLA via average token log-prob threshold; SST-2 via comparing 'positive' vs 'negative' after appending 'very'; RACE via highest avg token log-prob; DPRD via referent substitution) improve steadily over pre-training, indicating the LM acquires task-relevant functionality.

nodes.name: Ablation Studies
nodes.statement: Three ablations: (i) without auxiliary LM during fine-tuning helps NLI/QQP overall; (ii) replacing the Transformer with a single-layer 2048-unit LSTM drops average score by $5.6$; (iii) without pre-training accuracy drops by $14.8\%$ across tasks.

nodes.name: Auxiliary LM Helps Larger Datasets
nodes.statement: The auxiliary language modeling objective during fine-tuning helps larger datasets (e.g., NLI, QQP) but not smaller ones, suggesting the auxiliary loss acts as a regularizer most useful when ample supervised data is available.

nodes.name: Long-range Context Justifies BooksCorpus
nodes.statement: BooksCorpus is preferred over the 1B Word Benchmark because it preserves long stretches of contiguous text, enabling the generative model to condition on long-range information.

nodes.name: Transformer Inductive Bias Aids Transfer
nodes.statement: The structured attentional memory of the Transformer yields more stable zero-shot heuristic performance than an LSTM, suggesting its inductive bias is better suited for transfer.
